solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Firm with a thousand improves to get praises

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
mends means repairs or improves

explanation.surface: A business taking on a thousand staff makes improvements and earns compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend someone is to speak well of them, a verb synonym for lauding.

clue.text: Architectural construction is a newspaper feature

definitions.meaning: a regular article by a columnist

explanation.surface: A building element doubles as a press article.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar in a building and a regular piece in a newspaper share the same word.

clue.text: Scottish island home? Share accommodation maybe

parts.note: Muck is a small island in the Inner Hebrides
in means at home

explanation.surface: A home on a Scottish island might mean sharing your lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: Muck is one of the Small Isles off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in or share chores and quarters with others, as in muddling along together.

clue.text: Former cab-firm worker is full of joy

parts.note: ex means former
Uber is a ride-hailing taxi company
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: An ex-Uber driver is delighted to have quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the crossword's favourite insect, the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means bubbling over with high spirits and happiness.

clue.text: Medical specialists glamorised tots improperly

indicators.note: improperly suggests the letters of glamorised tots are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Doctors have glamorised small children in an unsuitable way.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors who specialise in the skin and its diseases.

clue.text: Facing a blast at university, wanting victory against head of department

parts.note: being up means in residence at university, in British usage
a win is a victory

indicators.note: head of signals taking the opening letter of the word department

explanation.surface: An academic is desperate to win a dispute with their head of department while under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing a blast' reads as weathering criticism, but it means heading into the wind. 'Wanting' and 'against' merely link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Going into the wind means facing its gusts head on, a literal paraphrase.

clue.text: Briefly visit work that's in fix

indicators.note: in means the work is placed inside the fix

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A quick visit about a job that has got into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' suggests a predicament, but it is PIN; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To call round for a short, informal stay.

clue.text: Straightforwardness that avoids extremes is taken for granted

indicators.note: avoiding extremes means dropping the outermost letters of the synonym

parts.note: simplicity means straightforwardness

explanation.surface: Plain dealing without exaggeration is something people assume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That avoids extremes' trims S and Y from SIMPLICITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Implied or understood without being stated, i.e. assumed.

clue.text: Rodent in boarding school room overlooking river

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking places one piece above the other

parts.note: a dorm is a dormitory, a shared bedroom at boarding school
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A rodent loose in a school dormitory with a view of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A small nocturnal rodent known for long hibernation.

clue.text: Alas, huge doctor troubles institution with students destined to be doctors?

definitions.text: institution with students destined to be doctors?

indicators.note: troubles suggests the letters of alas huge doctor are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sadly, a big physician causes problems for a medical school.
explanation.definitionFit: A postgraduate institution where students work towards higher degrees such as doctorates.

clue.text: Queen in delicate fabric right for coat

indicators.note: in means the queen piece is set inside the fabric

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A royal dressed in fine lace, just right for a coat she might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' looks like a garment, but it is a coating: varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a glossy varnish applied as a protective layer, i.e. a finish or covering.

clue.text: Decorate again, one way or the other

indicators.note: the phrase says the entry reads the same whichever direction you take it

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Redecorating a room, whichever way you go about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry is a palindrome, so 'one way or the other' is the whole wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging fresh wallpaper is a way of redecorating a room for a second time.

clue.text: Grass one found in Hampton Court feature

indicators.note: found in means the numeral sits inside the feature

parts.note: Hampton Court Palace near London has a famous hedge maze
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single blade of grass discovered within the grounds of Hampton Court.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampton Court is a royal palace near London whose hedge maze is famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is a cereal plant, and cereals belong botanically to the grass family.

clue.text: Movement — see nanna do it awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of nanna do it are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch grandma attempt a dance movement, clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' is a musical one, not a dance step.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderately slow tempo marking also names a section of a symphony or sonata, a musical movement.

clue.text: Fellow in business who cheats on his wife?

definitions.meaning: a businessman, someone handling commercial matters
punningly, a husband who has extramarital liaisons

explanation.surface: A businessman who is unfaithful to his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs means business dealings, and also illicit romances, so the phrase fits both senses.

clue.text: Adamant conclusion to prayer beginning to touch the heavens above

parts.note: firm means adamant
amen is said at the end of a prayer

indicators.note: beginning to signals the opening letter of the word touch

explanation.surface: A determined end to prayer reaches up towards the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the sky, poetically the heavens.

clue.text: Excited husband being embraced chirped

indicators.note: being embraced means the husband letter is enclosed by the other word

parts.note: trilled means sang in a warbling, birdlike way

explanation.surface: A delighted husband, hugged, chirps happily.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilled means delighted and excited.

clue.text: Road goes round country, coming to north European city

indicators.note: goes round means the road surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a lane is a minor road
USA is a country

explanation.surface: A road loops through the countryside towards a northern European city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss city on Lake Geneva, home of the International Olympic Committee.

clue.text: Conversation of two people getting pumped up?

definitions.text: Conversation of two people getting pumped up?

parts.words: Conversation of two people getting pumped up?
parts.note: an intimate talk between two people, with a pun on the organ that pumps blood

explanation.surface: Two people talking themselves into excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate, candid talk between two people; the pump is the organ in each chest.

clue.text: Dancer has oomph — behold this person!

parts.note: SA is sex appeal, oomph
lo is an old word for look or behold
me is the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: A dancer with great allure invites you to look at them.
explanation.walkthrough: SA (sex appeal) is crossword shorthand for oomph or 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical figure famous for the dance of the seven veils.

clue.text: Jumper — the one that jumped over the moon maybe?

definitions.meaning: a knitted sweater, the British sense of jumper

definitions.text: the one that jumped over the moon maybe?
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme a cow jumped over the moon; this is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: A jumper and the nursery-rhyme cow that leapt over the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is British for a sweater; 'Hey Diddle Diddle' has a cow jumping over the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover, and also a Channel Islands breed of dairy cow.

clue.text: One taken in by awful conman is suffering from sleep deficit

indicators.note: taken in by means the numeral is held within the other letters
awful signals that conman and is are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A victim deceived by a dreadful con artist is losing sleep over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in by' suggests being fooled by a swindler; here it is a container signal, and 'awful' is the anagram indicator, with 'is' part of the fodder rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chronically unable to sleep; used adjectivally it describes a person lacking rest.

clue.text: Iberian invaders in desolate areas

definitions.meaning: the North African Muslims who conquered much of Spain from 711

explanation.surface: Conquerors of Spain found in bleak wild country.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval conquerors of Spain share their name with bleak upland heaths.

clue.text: Time to protect a very small plant

indicators.note: to protect means the outer word wraps around the inner letters

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
a small v is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Taking time to shelter a tiny seedling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very small' looks like a description of the plant; it is V, the lowercase abbreviation of 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: A succulent with spiky leaves from the Americas, the source of tequila and sisal.

clue.text: Row not allowed as feature of ball game

parts.note: a line is a row
out means ruled out or not permitted

explanation.surface: An argument being banned at a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but is a line. A line-out is a rugby restart where players line up for a throw-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby set piece in which forwards line up to contest a throw from touch.

clue.text: Cool set, unconventional cats

indicators.note: unconventional suggests the letters of cool set are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A trendy, eccentric bunch of jazz cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' plays on hip slang for cool people; here they are real wild cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted wild felines of Central and South America, a specific kind of cat.

clue.text: Untidy doctor not male to be elegant

indicators.note: not signals the male letter is removed from the word for untidy

parts.note: messy means untidy

explanation.surface: A scruffy physician who is no gentleman tries to look smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not male' removes M from MESSY, leaving ESSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartly or formally attired; stylish in appearance.

clue.text: Express grief, drinking coffee — cups and saucers may be so noisy

definitions.text: cups and saucers may be so noisy

indicators.note: drinking means the outer word takes the coffee inside it

parts.note: to cry is to express grief
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: Weeping over a coffee while crockery rattles nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a rattling din, as crockery knocked together does.
